game.name: Pogo Rogue
game.short_description: Bounce to the top in this skill based, roguelite action-platformer! Collect powerful items, pick unique weapons, and fight off a variety of enemies while navigating around with a fun, difficult, and unique movement system. Are you up for the challenge?

placements.verbal_evidence: I'm going to, you know, proudly put Pogo, uh, Rogue as a, uh, as a cute little Btier.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 3 (2025)
commentary.summary: Pogo Rogue is a free action roguelike where you ride a pogo stick up through levels, using your weapon's recoil to propel yourself. He first played it in early access, found the precise controls too hard and the game too thin, and expected to give it a C. After replaying the full release he found it much more forgiving, with more roguelike content and a big hub. He places it in B tier as a small, charming game with a unique twist, and praises the developers for making it approachable.
praise: Unique pogo-stick climbing gimmick that defines the whole game
Full release is much more forgiving, with more room for mistakes (likely bigger levels and less annoying enemies)
Many weapons that feel very different because each gives different propulsion
Abilities (hat that shoots, jetpack, propeller) drastically change gameplay
Added hub world with lots to do
Free to play, which he finds remarkable for the quality
criticism: Controls are very precise and hard to get used to, even after the difficulty reduction
Early access version was too hard and not enthralling enough
Many players will try it for a few minutes and drop it due to inherent pogo difficulty
Hub world is slow to navigate on a pogo stick
unique_points: Downwell-inverted concept: shoot to propel yourself upward while damaging enemies below
Game relies heavily on its one main gimmick
Difficulty comes from the nature of the control mechanic rather than cheap design
commentary.quote: a cute little Btier... very simple, very small little game, but has a unique twist
design_criteria: Difficulty and approachability: reduced in the release via more room for error
Weapon diversity: different propulsion effects per weapon
Ability variety: abilities strongly alter gameplay
Meta-progression/hub: added hub world with content
Uniqueness of core gimmick: pogo mechanic is the hook
Scope: small game with limited content
commentary.rerank_note: Originally expected to give it C after early access; replaying the full release moved it up to B.

community.one_liner: A free, student-made 2D roguelite action-platformer where you ascend a factory by constantly bouncing on a pogo stick, using procedurally generated weapons, passives and active items.
community.consensus_summary: Pogo Rogue is a small, free Windows-only game from Bounce Back Games, made by University of Utah Division of Games students. It has a Very Positive Steam rating (196 positive of 213 reviews, about 92%). Players praise the tight, skill-based pogo movement, the addictive one-more-run loop and the fact that it costs nothing. The main friction is a steep learning curve for the movement and early difficulty, plus modest content length. It left Early Access in November 2024 with a final content drop, and the team said most members had moved on, so only occasional bug fixes were expected. Community discussion is sparse and there are no critic reviews, so the picture rests mostly on a few hundred Steam reviews and forum posts.
best_things: The pogo-stick movement system is distinctive and, once learned, feels natural and very satisfying (wall jumping and speedrunning get specific mention)
Addictive one-more-run loop; several reviewers say they lost hours unexpectedly
Variety of weapons, passive items, active items and synergy items keeps runs different thanks to procedural generation
Bosses are singled out as a highlight by long-time players (one reviewer with several hundred hours)
Free to play, and reviewers say the quality is well above what a free student game should be
Runs well on low-end hardware, Linux via Proton and Steam Deck; tiny install (around 100MB, i3 and 4GB RAM minimum)
worst_things: Steep, unforgiving early difficulty; one reviewer dropped after many deaths following only two boss kills
Movement takes a long time to learn before it clicks, and the tutorial does not fully explain it
Some players get stuck on level-navigation obstacles (for example a reviewer who could not work out how to get past a metal ceiling in the first area) and leave a negative review
Reports of bugs on the Steam forum: a solid-box hive item breaking, and the Constructus enemy leaving its arena
Occasional lag spikes reported on Steam Deck despite generally good performance
Windows only on Steam (no native Mac or Linux build)
improvements: Better onboarding and tutorials for the pogo movement and first-area obstacles
Control scheme options and more rebinding and controller-related settings were requested on the forum
Ability to swap active items, requested by players
More content: at least one reviewer calls it a little short
Balance fixes for exploits; a forum thread discusses a game-breaking strategy
Continued bug-fix support, since active development ended with the full release
unique_things: Entire movement is built around a constantly bouncing pogo stick, which makes it closer to a precision platformer than a typical combat-first roguelite
Skill-based difficulty: player execution matters more than build luck
Synergy items that combine active items, with free switching between a synergy item and its components
Hub area with NPCs such as Pogosmith and a Traveling Salesman, plus unlockable characters
Factory setting and a student-team pedigree from the University of Utah Division of Games
tedious_or_disliked: Dying repeatedly while learning the movement before the game starts to feel fun
Hitting a difficulty wall at the boss stage after the early areas
Confusing early-level navigation without clear guidance
Early Access-era difficulty was high enough that the developers removed bats from area 1 and raised starting health in October 2024 patches
divisive_points: Difficulty: some find it a rewarding skill curve, others bounce off early
Content amount: praised for depth by high-hour players but called a little short by others
Steam Deck performance: several praise it, one recent review reports lag spikes
community.reception_notes: Early Access launched in April 2024, with major content updates on Oct 9, 12, 18 and 23, 2024 (new items, weapons, NPCs, characters, hub, balance changes and achievements). Full 1.0 release was on Nov 20, 2024, adding 8 passives, 4 weapons and 2 bosses. The developers stated the game is a free student project, most of the team had moved on, and future updates would be limited. The last visible forum post was June 2025, and Steam reviews continue to trickle in into 2026, so the game has a small, still-active audience. No critic coverage was found, Metacritic has a page with no critic score and too few user ratings, and there is no OpenCritic entry found. Sales data is not applicable because the game is free (SteamSpy estimates 0 to 20,000 owners). Research limitation: the web search budget was exhausted, so no Reddit or outlet reviews were found and Reddit could not be fetched; the picture relies on Steam store, reviews, forum and announcements.
